Text: Trump administration bans new Chinese humanoid robots The US and China are locked in a race to the lead the world in robotics and artificial intelligence.
Summarized_Data: – The Trump administration on Tuesday announced a ban on new foreign-made humanoid robot imports to the US over "unacceptable risks" to the country's national security. The Federal Communications Commission also banned the import of power inverters—a device used in data centers and solar panels—which it said could also pose a risk to the US economy. The FCC has added the items to its Covered List—a register of goods and services that are deemed a risk to US national security. The ban applies to new foreign-produced advanced robotic devices and power inverters and does not prevent the sale or import of any existing models that had been previously authorised by the FCC. The FCC cited concerns that the use of foreign-made inverters could allow overseas firms to turn them off, steal data, facilitate remote access and surveillance by "foreign government actors, or be otherwise exploited through a cyberattack." China's exports have come under intense scrutiny by the US as the Trump administration attempts to address trade imbalances with the world's second largest economy.

Text: Ghana mourns its tallest man - a 'generous and popular giant' Sulemana Abdul Samed, who was diagnosed with gigantism several years ago, has died at the age of 33.
Summarized_Data: – Sulemana Abdul Samed, Ghana's tallest man, has prompted an outpouring of grief especially in the north of the country where his height had made him a local celebrity. The 33 year old died in hospital on Monday in the northern city of Tamale, about 100 miles south of his home village of Gambaga, where he had been admitted because sores on his legs had become infected.''From when he died until now a lot of people are still coming to the house to find out what exactly happened,'' a relative, Sulemana Abdul Kudus, has told the BBC.''Anywhere he found himself in the country and they asked him, he would say he is from Gambaga and people knew that was where the tallest man was from.'' Text: Lindsey Graham remembered by Trump as 'giant of the US Senate' at funeral The US president was among several dignitaries who attended the service for the late lawmaker, who died earlier this month.
Summarized_Data: – President Donald Trump has remembered Lindsey Graham as a "giant of the United States Senate" at the late lawmaker's funeral in Washington. In his eulogy, Trump also called Graham, who died earlier this month at the age of 71, a "true American original, who left us much too soon." Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also attended the funeral on Tuesday to pay their respects to Graham, who was a major supporter of both countries. Trump recounted an episode in which he publicly shared Graham's phone number at a 2015 campaign event, after the senator lobbed a profane insult his way. "His phone exploded," Trump told the mourners assembled in the nave of the cathedral. "It was Lindsey who had the last laugh," he continued. Graham had just returned home from a trip to Kyiv in Ukraine to meet with President Zelensky when he died of an "aortic dissection"—a tear in the heart's main artery.

Text: Zelensky and Netanyahu meet Trump as wars in Ukraine and Iran drag on The two leaders were in Washington to attend the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham, a staunch supporter of Israel and advocate for US aid to Ukraine.
Summarized_Data: – President Trump has held separate meetings with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, which the White House described as "positive and productive." The two leaders were in Washington to attend the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham, a staunch supporter of Israel and advocate for US aid to Ukraine, who died earlier this month. Zelensky and Trump discussed Kyiv's hope that the US would help bolster its air defenses, although no formal commitment has so far been announced. Netanyahu, for his part, arrived at a time when US-Israel ties have been frayed by diverging views on Iran. Zelensky was expected to press Trump to follow through on a promise he made at this month's NATO summit to grant Ukraine a license to produce Patriot interceptor missiles. Ukraine has long sought American Patriot missiles, which Kyiv says could be used to defend Ukrainian cities from escalating Russian drone and ballistic missile attacks across the country. Trump posted on Truth Social that the meeting "went very well!" In a post on X, Zelensky thanked the US president for "everything we do together to protect the lives of Ukrainians."

Text: Bystander video shows teen lifeguard's dramatic ocean rescue The 16-year-old lifeguard rescued a 10-year-old who had been swept offshore at a California beach.
Summarized_Data: – Video captured by a bystander shows the moment 16-year-old rookie lifeguard Ryder Williams rescued a 10-year-old boy from the ocean at Seabright State Beach in Santa Cruz, California. The child had been swept about 15 yards (13.7m) offshore when Williams reached him, with several beachgoers also joining the rescue. The operation lasted just over two minutes. President Donald Trump has since invited Williams to the White House to receive a high civilian honor.

Text: US walks out of UN Security Council meeting during France's remarks
Summarized_Data: – The US delegation walked out of a UN Security Council meeting on Monday, in protest at comments made by France that compared Washington's voting on human rights to that of authoritarian states. The diplomatic row was initially sparked last week, when the US joined North Korea and Russia in voting against extending Volker Turk's term as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights. After the vote on Friday, France's UN mission criticized the US and compared it to North Korea and Russia. "The US used to be a beacon of human rights. Not anymore," it posted on X. In response, US ambassador Mike Waltz accused France of voting for a human rights chief who had been "lecturing" democratic countries while "cozying up to the world's worst oppressors", without elaborating on what he meant. The US team's walkout came while France's ambassador Jerome Bonnafont was speaking during an emergency Security Council meeting on Russia's war in Ukraine. US ambassador Dan Negrea said the delegation would continue to make similar protests until France "renounces their condescending and disrespectful rhetoric." The fight over Turk's second term, which was passed with 144 states in favor, 10 against and 13 abstentions, reflects tensions between Washington and the United Nations.

Text: Wildfires in south-west France flare up as region braces for new 40C heatwave
Summarized_Data: – "The fire is like David against Goliath," said Eric Brocardi, spokesman of the national firefighters' federation. Four of his colleagues had died in recent weeks across France, he said, and 2,000 had been deployed in the Gironde to contain the flames, which for days have ravaged the countryside between the coastline and Bordeaux. The French city of Bordeaux is not currently under threat, according to officials, despite the fact that one of the wildfires burning on Monday came only 9 miles from the city's periphery. Interior Minister Laurent Nuez said that 184 people had been arrested since 6 July in connection with the fires.
